stem: A ticketing company is building an order system for customers in North America, Europe and Asia. It needs a relational schema with SQL, transactions that are strongly consistent everywhere, and write capacity that grows by adding resources rather than by moving to a bigger single primary server. Which database should the team choose?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with cross-region read replicas, which serve reads close to users while one primary takes all writes
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with read pool instances, which add read nodes on demand while the cluster stays in a single region
Spanner with a multi-region instance configuration, which shards data automatically and keeps transactions strongly consistent
Bigtable with clusters in three regions and replication, which spreads reads and writes across clusters in every continent

stem: An energy company collects a reading every few seconds from two million smart meters. The application writes very high volumes of small records and reads them back by meter ID and time range with single-digit millisecond latency. The developers already use the Apache HBase API. Which service fits best?

choices.text: Firestore, with one document per reading stored in a collection per meter and a composite index on the timestamp field
Bigtable, with a row key that starts with the meter ID followed by a timestamp so each meter's readings sit together
BigQuery, with a table partitioned by day and clustered by meter ID so that range scans on recent readings stay quick
Cloud SQL for MySQL, with a table indexed on meter ID and timestamp and several read replicas for the dashboard queries

stem: A firm is moving an internal finance application from its data center to Google Cloud. The application uses Microsoft SQL Server, and the team wants Google to handle backups, patching and high availability failover without changing the database engine. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for SQL Server, a managed instance that keeps the same engine and adds automated backups and a standby for failover
BigQuery with a dataset per database, a managed warehouse that runs the application's T-SQL transactions without changes
Spanner with the GoogleSQL dialect, a managed database whose schema accepts SQL Server tables after a direct backup restore
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, a managed cluster whose engine takes SQL Server queries after the schema is imported unchanged

stem: A retailer's order application runs on PostgreSQL. Managers want reports that run heavy analytical queries directly on the live order data, without a nightly export, and without slowing down the order transactions. The team wants to keep using standard PostgreSQL clients. Which service should the team choose?

choices.text: Bigtable, with the order data copied into it so that reports can scan wide rows by order date with low latency
Memorystore for Redis, with report results cached in memory so that repeated analytical queries return quickly
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with a scheduled export to Cloud Storage and a BigQuery load job that runs every night
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, using its columnar engine and read pool instances to run the analytical queries on live data

stem: A start-up is building a mobile and web app that stores user profiles and posts as JSON-like documents. The team wants a serverless database that scales automatically without capacity planning, charges for actual use, and works with the Firebase SDKs. Which database should they pick?

choices.text: Bigtable, a wide-column database whose cluster nodes are sized up front and adjusted when traffic changes
Memorystore for Redis, an in-memory store whose hashes hold each profile and post as a set of key fields
Firestore, a serverless document database that scales automatically and integrates with the Firebase platform
Cloud SQL for MySQL, a relational instance with a JSON column type and storage that grows automatically

stem: Analysts at a media company need to run ad hoc SQL queries over several hundred terabytes of clickstream data and connect a BI tool to the results. The team does not want to provision, patch or scale any database servers. Which service should hold the data?

choices.text: Spanner, with a regional instance configuration whose compute capacity is raised before the reporting runs
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with the largest machine type and read replicas added for each group of analysts
Bigtable, with an instance cluster sized for the full data set and its nodes scaled out during peak query hours
BigQuery, a serverless data warehouse that separates storage from compute and runs SQL queries without servers

stem: A web application on Compute Engine stores user sessions in a Cloud SQL database, and page loads slow down under heavy traffic. The developers already use an open source Redis client library and want a managed in-memory store that answers in under a millisecond, reached over a private IP in their VPC. What should they use?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, a managed Redis-protocol store that the existing client can use with no code changes
Firestore in Native mode, a managed document store that the existing client reaches through its MongoDB API
A Cloud SQL read replica, a managed copy of the database that the existing client reaches over the same private IP
Bigtable with an SSD cluster, a managed wide-column store that the existing client reaches through its HBase API

stem: A logistics company runs dozens of services that produce and consume events with Apache Kafka client libraries and Kafka Connect, on a self-managed cluster. They want Google Cloud to run the cluster for them without rewriting producers or consumers. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, whose streams store the events and accept the existing Kafka producer calls with no code changes
Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka, which runs Kafka clusters that the existing Kafka clients connect to
Pub/Sub, whose topics and subscriptions receive the existing Kafka producer and consumer calls with no code changes
Dataflow, whose streaming jobs act as Kafka brokers that the existing Kafka clients connect to as their bootstrap servers

stem: A game studio wants to collect gameplay events from thousands of game servers, enrich and aggregate them in near real time, and write the results into BigQuery. The team wants fully managed services with no clusters to run. Which TWO services should they combine? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, to hold the raw events in memory and run the enrichment and aggregation step in the cache
Filestore, to collect the events as files on a shared NFS share that BigQuery reads directly as the source table
Dataflow, to run a streaming Apache Beam pipeline that reads the events, transforms them and writes to BigQuery
Cloud SQL for MySQL, to stage every raw event in a table and run scheduled stored procedures that load BigQuery
Pub/Sub, to receive the events asynchronously from the game servers and buffer them for downstream processing

stem: A media team runs a rendering application on a managed instance group of Linux VMs and on a GKE cluster. All VMs and Pods must read and write the same POSIX file tree at the same time over NFS, with file locking. Which storage should the team provision?

choices.text: A Cloud Storage bucket mounted with Cloud Storage FUSE, which provides file locking and full POSIX semantics
A Filestore instance, whose NFS file share every VM and Pod can mount read-write at the same time
A Memorystore for Redis instance, whose keys each hold one file so that every VM and Pod reads the same data
A zonal Persistent Disk attached to every VM, which mounts it read-write as a shared POSIX file system

stem: An engineering firm is moving Windows file servers to Google Cloud. Users on Windows desktops map the shares as network drives over SMB, and Linux build servers mount other volumes over NFS. The firm wants one fully managed service that provides both protocols. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, mounting its parallel file system on both the Windows desktops and the build servers
Cloud Storage with Cloud Storage FUSE, mounting each bucket as a network drive on the Windows desktops over SMB
Filestore, using the regional tier for continuous availability and mounting the shares from Windows over SMB
Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, which provides managed volumes over SMB and NFS protocols with snapshots and backups

stem: A research lab trains large machine learning models on hundreds of GPU VMs and GKE nodes. Training needs a shared POSIX file system that delivers very high aggregate throughput and IOPS to all nodes at once, and data sets are staged from Cloud Storage. Which storage service is designed for this?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, a fully managed parallel file system for AI and HPC with transfers to and from Cloud Storage
Cloud Storage with the Nearline storage class, a bucket that every GPU node reads through the JSON API during training
Filestore with the basic tier, a legacy managed NFS share for basic file sharing that every GPU node mounts at once
Memorystore for Redis with five replicas, an in-memory store whose keys hold the training files for every GPU node

stem: A finance team continuously uploads transaction exports to a bucket and runs an analysis job on them about once a month. The files must stay online with fast access, and the team wants to lower at-rest storage cost without paying for retrievals more often than needed. Which storage class should the bucket use by default?

choices.text: Standard storage, which is meant for data read less than once a year and has a 365-day minimum storage duration
Nearline storage, which is meant for data read or modified about once a month and has a 30-day minimum storage duration
Archive storage, which is meant for data read about once a month and has offline retrieval that takes several hours
Coldline storage, which is meant for data read or modified several times every week and has no minimum storage duration

stem: A hospital must keep scanned records for ten years for regulatory reasons. The records are almost never read, but during an audit some files must be readable at once. The team is evaluating Archive storage. Which TWO statements about Archive storage are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An object deleted or replaced before it has been stored for 365 days is charged as if it was stored for 365 days
Objects in Archive storage must first be restored to Standard storage, which can take several hours per object
Archive storage can be used only in single-region buckets, so it cannot be combined with dual-region redundancy
Archive storage cannot be set as a bucket's default class, so each object must get the class when it is uploaded
Objects in Archive storage are readable within milliseconds, with no restore step before the data can be accessed

stem: A bucket holds 2 TB of log files in Standard storage. An engineer changes the bucket's default storage class to Coldline to save money, but a week later every existing object still shows the Standard class. What explains this, and how can the engineer change the existing objects?

choices.text: The default class is ignored while uniform bucket-level access is on; disable it so the existing objects can take the new default class
The change takes up to 30 days to reach existing objects; wait for the background conversion to finish before checking the class again
The bucket is in a multi-region, where Coldline is not supported; recreate the bucket in a single region and then copy the objects there
The default class applies only to objects added later; rewrite the existing objects with gcloud storage objects update and --storage-class

stem: An engineer must upload a local directory of about 200 GB with many subdirectories from a workstation into gs://proj-media-raw, keeping the folder structure, and the objects should be stored as Nearline. The network link is good. Which command is the simplest correct choice?

choices.text: bq load --source_format=CSV proj_media.raw ./media/* --storage_class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp ./media gs://proj-media-raw --no-clobber --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp --recursive ./media gs://proj-media-raw --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage buckets create gs://proj-media-raw --placement=./media --default-storage-class=NEARLINE

stem: A company keeps 400 TB of product images in Amazon S3 and wants to move them to Cloud Storage, then copy new and changed files every night until the cut-over. The team wants a managed service that retries failures and checks integrity, without writing scripts or running copy servers. What should they use?

choices.text: A BigQuery load job from the S3 bucket each night, followed by an export of the loaded data to Cloud Storage
A Compute Engine VM that runs gcloud storage rsync from the S3 bucket every night through a cron job on the VM
Storage Transfer Service, with an S3 source, a Cloud Storage destination and a daily schedule for the transfer job
Transfer Appliance, shipped to the S3 region so that the images are copied onto it and loaded into Cloud Storage

stem: An analyst runs bq load to load CSV files from gs://acme-sales-us/2026/*.csv into the table sales.daily. The bucket is in the US multi-region, and the sales dataset was created in the europe-west1 region. The load job fails before reading any rows. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The locations of source and target differ; copy the objects to storage colocated with the target, or use a US dataset
CSV loads need an explicit schema because auto-detection reads JSON files alone; pass a local JSON schema file to the job
bq load needs Storage Transfer Service to move objects from a bucket into BigQuery; create a transfer job for the files
A wildcard in a Cloud Storage URI is rejected by bq load; list the CSV files by name in a comma-separated set of URIs

stem: Each night a job drops a CSV file with one header row into gs://acme-orders/daily/. An engineer writes a bq load command that adds the file's rows to the existing table orders.history, which has a schema and holds years of data that must not be lost. Which TWO choices must the command make? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Pass --time_partitioning_type=DAY on each run so that the existing table is converted to daily partitions
Pass --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON so that the header line is read as the names of the columns
Pass --replace so that the existing schema is kept and new rows are written alongside the old data
Use --skip_leading_rows=1 so that the header row is not loaded as a data row into the table
Append the rows, by passing --noreplace or by leaving out --replace, so that existing rows stay

stem: A payments company stores transaction receipts in Cloud Storage. The bucket must keep serving reads and writes with the same bucket name if one region goes down, the data must stay in two regions the company chooses, and newly written objects must be copied to the second region within 15 minutes. Which TWO settings meet these needs when the bucket is created? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A single-region location, with Autoclass enabled so that objects move to colder classes in a second region over time
The recovery point objective set to ASYNC_TURBO, which turns on turbo replication for the dual-region bucket
A multi-region location such as EU, with turbo replication enabled so that copies reach a second region in minutes
A single-region location, with Object Versioning enabled so that earlier versions of objects can be restored later
A dual-region location, either a predefined pair or a configurable dual-region whose two regions are set with --placement

stem: A logistics company is moving a legacy inventory application to Google Cloud. The application runs on a commercial Linux distribution, loads a vendor-supplied kernel driver at boot, and the vendor supports it only when it runs unmodified on a full operating system. The team wants to change as little as possible. Where should the team run the application?

choices.text: On a GKE Autopilot cluster, running the application as a Deployment with the vendor driver installed through an init container in each Pod
On Cloud Run, after packaging the application and its kernel driver into a container image that loads the driver when each instance starts
On Cloud Run functions, splitting the application into event-driven functions that call the vendor driver through a shared library at runtime
On Compute Engine VMs built from an image of that distribution, so the team controls the operating system, kernel modules and installed packages

stem: A small team has a stateless REST API packaged as a container image. It receives traffic only during office hours and none at night or on weekends. The team does not want to manage VMs or clusters and does not want to pay for compute while the API is idle. Which compute option should the team choose?

choices.text: A Cloud Run service deployed from the image, letting it scale to zero instances when no requests arrive
A regional managed instance group of small VMs running the container, autoscaled on average CPU utilization with a minimum of zero
A GKE Standard cluster with the cluster autoscaler enabled on its node pool, running the image as a Deployment behind a Service
An Agent Runtime deployment on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which runs the image in a fully managed environment

stem: A developer has built a customer-support AI agent and now needs to run it in production. The team wants a fully managed environment that deploys and scales the agent, keeps conversation state across turns, can store long-term memories about users, and provides tracing and logging, without the team operating servers. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Split each agent tool into a separate Cloud Run function and keep the conversation history in the instance memory of each function
Deploy the agent to Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and use Agent Platform Sessions and Memory Bank for state
Package the agent as a container and run it on a Compute Engine managed instance group, storing session state in a Cloud SQL database the team manages
Run the agent on a GKE Standard cluster with a StatefulSet that stores each conversation on the Persistent Disk of its Pod

stem: An engineer created a reporting VM with a script copied from an old wiki that included --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE and --no-restart-on-failure. Last night Google performed host maintenance, and this morning the VM is in the TERMINATED state and nobody restarted it. The VM uses a general-purpose machine type with no GPUs. How should the engineer change the VM's host maintenance policy?

choices.text: Enable deletion protection on the VM so that Compute Engine can no longer stop or terminate it during host maintenance events
Recreate the VM as a Spot VM so that Compute Engine moves it to another host automatically whenever maintenance is scheduled
Set the maintenance behavior to migrate (live migration) and turn automatic restart back on so host errors also restart the VM
Add a snapshot schedule to the boot disk so that the VM is recreated from the latest snapshot after each maintenance event

stem: A data team plans to use Spot VMs to cut the cost of a nightly transcoding fleet. Which statements about Spot VMs are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Spot VMs are covered by the Compute Engine SLA at a reduced uptime percentage, so short outages caused by preemption earn service credits
Spot VMs are priced by bidding: you set a maximum hourly bid, and the VM is preempted whenever the market price rises above your bid
Spot VMs cannot live migrate during host maintenance and cannot be configured to restart automatically when a host event occurs
Spot VMs keep running for at most 24 hours, after which Compute Engine always stops them, even when spare capacity is still available
Compute Engine can preempt a Spot VM at any time to reclaim capacity, and its termination action decides whether the VM is stopped or deleted

stem: A media startup renders video frames pulled from a work queue. Each frame is independent and can simply be retried, and the goal is the lowest compute cost. When Compute Engine reclaims a worker VM, the team wants a replacement worker created automatically from the same configuration without anyone stepping in. What should the team set up?

choices.text: Standard VMs on a sole-tenant node group, with the automatic restart policy enabled so that crashed workers come back
An unmanaged instance group of Spot VMs, each created by hand, with a load balancer health check pointed at the group
One large Spot VM with automatic restart turned on, so that Compute Engine restarts it on another host after preemption
A managed instance group whose instance template uses the Spot provisioning model, so the group recreates preempted VMs

stem: A team creates Spot VMs each night with gcloud compute instances create ... --provisioning-model=SPOT. After preemptions, dozens of VMs remain in the TERMINATED state, and their boot disks keep adding to the bill. The team wants preempted VMs to disappear on their own. Which change should they make to the create command?

choices.text: Add --no-restart-on-failure so that Compute Engine does not try to bring the Spot VM back after it is preempted
Add --instance-termination-action=DELETE so that Compute Engine deletes each Spot VM when it preempts it
Replace --provisioning-model=SPOT with --preemptible so that preempted VMs are removed after 24 hours of running
Add --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE so that preempted VMs are terminated permanently instead of only stopped

stem: A finance team runs a third-party risk engine licensed per vCPU; they own licenses for exactly 6 vCPUs. Load tests show the engine needs 6 vCPUs and about 30 GB of memory. The closest predefined type, n2-standard-8, would need 8 licenses. What should the cloud engineer create?

choices.text: A VM with an N2 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM with the predefined n2-highmem-4 machine type and 32 GB of memory
A VM with a C3 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM on a sole-tenant node with 8 vCPUs, reserving 2 vCPUs for later

stem: An in-memory analytics product is licensed per vCPU, and the team has budgeted for 4 vCPUs. The data set needs 64 GB of RAM on a single VM, and CPU usage is low. The team plans to use the N2 machine series. Which configuration meets both constraints?

choices.text: The predefined n2-highmem-8 type with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB, then license only 4 of the vCPUs in the product
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, created with the extended memory feature
An E2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, since E2 has no memory-per-vCPU limit
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of memory, the most memory a 4-vCPU custom type allows

stem: A team runs a self-managed PostgreSQL server on one Compute Engine VM in us-central1-a. Management now requires that the database survive the loss of that zone with no loss of committed data, and a standby VM can be kept stopped in us-central1-b. Which storage design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with a snapshot schedule every hour, and create a new disk in us-central1-b from the latest snapshot
Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with Asynchronous Replication to europe-west1, and fail over to a VM created in that region
Keep the data on Local SSD disks in RAID 0 for speed, and copy the database files to a Cloud Storage bucket in the same region every fifteen minutes
Keep the data on a Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability or regional Persistent Disk volume replicated to both zones, and attach it to the standby VM on failover

stem: A MySQL VM keeps 400 GB of data on a balanced Persistent Disk and is limited by disk IOPS. To get the IOPS it needs, the team would have to grow the disk to several terabytes it will never fill. The VM's machine series supports Hyperdisk. Which option raises IOPS without paying for unused capacity?

choices.text: Move the data to a Hyperdisk Throughput volume and raise its IOPS level separately from its size
Resize the balanced Persistent Disk to several terabytes, since disk IOPS scale with its capacity
Move the data to a Hyperdisk Balanced volume and set the provisioned IOPS independently of its size
Move the data to Local SSD disks, which deliver higher IOPS than any network-attached disk type

stem: An inference fleet of 400 Compute Engine VMs must load the same 150 GB of model weights at startup. The weights never change between releases, and startup time matters. The team wants one copy of the data that every VM reads directly as a disk. Which disk type should they use?

choices.text: A Hyperdisk ML volume, loaded once and then attached in read-only mode to every VM in the fleet
A Hyperdisk Balanced volume in multi-writer mode, attached to every VM in the fleet at the same time
A Hyperdisk Throughput volume, attached to one VM that copies the weights to the others over the network
A Hyperdisk Extreme volume, attached in read-write mode to every VM in the fleet for the highest IOPS

stem: A team plans to add Local SSD to a Microsoft SQL Server VM. Which statements about Local SSD are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Local SSD cannot be used as a boot volume, so the VM still needs a durable boot disk such as Hyperdisk or Persistent Disk
Local SSD is synchronously replicated to a second zone, so its data survives the failure of the zone that hosts the VM
Local SSD data is kept when a Spot VM is preempted, because the disks stay attached to the stopped VM on the same host
Local SSD disks can be detached from a running VM and attached to another VM in the same zone, like a Hyperdisk volume
Local SSD gives the fastest block storage but is temporary, so it suits scratch data and caches such as SQL Server tempdb

stem: A web tier runs in a managed instance group created from the instance template web-tmpl-v1, which uses e2-medium. The team wants new and existing VMs to use n2-standard-2, but finds no way to edit the machine type of web-tmpl-v1. What is the correct approach?

choices.text: Delete web-tmpl-v1 while the group is still using it, then recreate a template with the same name and the new machine type
Run gcloud compute instance-templates update web-tmpl-v1 with the new machine type, then restart the VMs in the group one by one
Stop each VM in the group, change its machine type to n2-standard-2 directly, and start it again so the template no longer matters
Create a new template, such as web-tmpl-v2 based on the old one with n2-standard-2, and roll it out to the group with an update

stem: A managed instance group autoscales on average CPU utilization with a 60% target. Each new VM spends about 4 minutes installing packages at boot, with high CPU, before the app serves traffic. During every spike the group overshoots and adds far more VMs than needed. Which autoscaler setting should be adjusted?

choices.text: Configure scale-in controls with a small maximum allowed reduction, so that the group adds fewer VMs during each spike
Set the initialization period to about 240 seconds, so that scale-out ignores data from VMs that are still starting up
Raise the target CPU utilization to 95%, so that the high CPU of booting VMs no longer triggers additional scale-out
Set the stabilization period to 4 minutes, so that the autoscaler waits that long before it adds any new VMs to the group

stem: Workers in a managed instance group process messages from a Pub/Sub subscription. The group autoscales on average CPU utilization, and the team set the minimum number of instances to 0 so it would be empty overnight when the queue is empty, yet at least one VM always keeps running. How should the team reach zero instances when there is no work?

choices.text: Switch the signal to HTTP load balancing serving capacity, which reports zero usage once all requests have stopped
Add a scaling schedule with a capacity of 0 instances every night, which forces the group to delete all of its VMs
Scale on a Cloud Monitoring metric for the subscription's backlog of undelivered messages instead of CPU, keeping minimum at 0
Lower the CPU utilization target to 1%, so that the autoscaler sees even one idle VM as over target and removes it

stem: A retailer's web tier runs on Compute Engine. It must keep serving if an entire zone in us-east1 goes down, and VMs on which the web application has hung (while the VM itself still runs) must be replaced automatically. Which configuration meets these goals? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure application-based autohealing with a health check on the app's endpoint, so the group recreates unhealthy VMs
Rely on the load balancer's health check alone, since a failing backend health check makes the group recreate the VM
Keep automatic restart enabled in the VMs' host maintenance policy, so that Compute Engine restarts VMs whose app hangs
Put the VMs in an unmanaged instance group that contains VMs from all three zones of us-east1 behind the load balancer
Create a regional managed instance group so that the group's VMs are spread across several zones of us-east1

stem: A project's Linux VMs use SSH keys stored in project metadata. The security team wants contractors to get SSH access through IAM, without sudo, and to lose access automatically as soon as their IAM role is removed. Which actions should the cloud engineer take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add each contractor's public SSH key to the project metadata and set an expiry time on every key that is added
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to TRUE in the project metadata so that the project's VMs use OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osAdminLogin role so that they can log in to the VMs through OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 role so that they can manage SSH keys on the instances
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osLogin role on the project or on the specific VMs they need to reach

stem: A project still uses metadata-based SSH keys, and a dozen administrators have their keys in project metadata. One new VM processes payroll data and must accept only the two keys that the payroll team adds to that VM's own metadata. OS Login cannot be used yet. What should the engineer configure on the VM?

choices.text: Remove the dozen administrator keys from the project metadata, and add the two payroll keys to the project metadata instead
Create the payroll VM without a service account, so that the keys stored in project metadata are not copied onto the VM
Set the metadata key block-project-ssh-keys to TRUE on the payroll VM, and add the two payroll keys to its instance metadata
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to FALSE on the payroll VM, so that it reads only the keys stored in its own metadata

stem: An operations team set up VM Manager and a weekly patch deployment for 200 Ubuntu VMs. Patch compliance reports show up for every VM, but patch jobs fail on the VMs that have no external IP address; their subnet has no Cloud NAT and no proxy. What should the team do?

choices.text: Grant the OS Config agent's service account the Compute Admin role on the project, so it can download patches for the VMs
Recreate the failing VMs with external IP addresses, since VM Manager requires every managed VM to have a public address
Switch the patch deployment to OS inventory management, which installs updates without contacting package repositories
Give the VMs a path to package updates, such as Cloud NAT for the subnet or a local repository the VMs can reach

stem: A security team requires that a specific monitoring package be installed on every Linux VM labeled env=prod, and that it be reinstalled automatically if someone removes it. The team wants to use a VM Manager feature rather than writing its own tooling. Which feature should it use?

choices.text: OS policies, which describe the desired package state for the selected VMs and keep that state in place
A startup script in the instance metadata of each production VM that installs the package at every boot
OS inventory management, which collects and reports which packages are present on each selected VM
Patch deployments, which apply operating system updates to the selected VMs on a recurring schedule

stem: A research group will train a large recommendation model. The model is dominated by matrix multiplications, uses ultra-large embeddings, has no custom operations in its training loop, and is expected to train for weeks with large batch sizes. Which hardware should the cloud engineer plan for?

choices.text: GPUs attached to Compute Engine VMs, because GPUs are the only accelerator that Google Cloud offers for model training
High-CPU Compute Engine VMs, because large embeddings run best on general-purpose CPUs with plenty of cores
Cloud TPUs, because they suit models whose training loop relies on many custom PyTorch operations run on CPUs
Cloud TPUs, because they are ASICs built for large matrix operations and suit large models that train for weeks

stem: A platform team lets developers create their own projects. Each new project must be paid for by the company's central Cloud Billing account, but developers must not see invoices, change payment methods or manage who has access to that billing account. Which role should the developers get on the billing account, in addition to Project Creator on their folder?

choices.text: Billing Account Creator (`roles/billing.creator`), which allows creating new self-serve billing accounts at the organization level
Billing Account Administrator (`roles/billing.admin`), which allows linking projects and also manages the account's settings
Billing Account User (`roles/billing.user`), which allows linking projects to the account and has very restricted permissions
Billing Account Viewer (`roles/billing.viewer`), which allows reading cost data and transactions recorded on the billing account

stem: The finance department wants two analysts to see the costs, transactions and payment documents of the company's Cloud Billing account. They must not be able to link or unlink projects, create budgets or change any account settings. Which predefined role on the billing account fits this best?

choices.text: Project Billing Manager, which is granted on each project and lets the analysts view that project's invoices directly
Billing Account Viewer, which gives read access to cost and payment information without managing the billing account
Billing Account Costs Manager, which shows cost information and also lets the analysts create, edit and delete budgets
Billing Account User, which lets the analysts attach projects to the account while hiding its payment information

stem: A FinOps engineer must create and edit budgets for every project on the billing account and set up the usage cost export to BigQuery. Security policy says the engineer must not link or unlink projects or manage who has access to the billing account. Which role should be granted on the billing account?

choices.text: Billing Account Costs Manager, which manages budgets and the export of cost data but cannot link projects or manage account properties
Billing Account Viewer, which reads cost data and transactions and can edit budgets that other administrators already created
Project Billing Costs Manager, which manages budgets and the cost export for every project linked to the billing account without project roles
Billing Account Administrator, which manages budgets and the export of cost data and also controls the account's role assignments

stem: A project owner wants a contractor to move the project `web-prod` from an old Cloud Billing account to a new one. The contractor must not get access to any resources in the project. Which roles give the contractor what is needed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Billing Account Viewer (`roles/billing.viewer`) on the new Cloud Billing account only
Project Editor (`roles/editor`) on the `web-prod` project to change its settings

stem: A team is building its first production network in a new project that has no VPC network yet. stem: A central network team keeps all subnets, routes and firewall rules in one project. Three departments each run VMs in their own project of the same organization. stem: A Shared VPC Admin attached an existing project to a host project as a service project and granted its admins Compute Network User on a shared subnet. stem: A hub VPC network is peered with spoke-a and with spoke-b, and all three use non-overlapping ranges. VMs in each spoke can reach VMs in the hub, but VMs in spoke-a cannot reach VMs in spoke-b. The team wants direct private connectivity between the two spokes. What should the team do?

stem: A company plans to connect its analytics VPC network to a partner's VPC network with VPC Network Peering. Which statements about VPC Network Peering are correct? (Select TWO)

stem: Frontend VMs run as frontend-sa and backend VMs run as backend-sa, both in one VPC network. Developers hold Compute Instance Admin and often edit VMs, including their network tags. stem: The security team must block inbound RDP (TCP 3389) from the internet to every VM in all projects under the Production folder. stem: A small company must connect a branch office to its VPC network this week. Expected traffic is a few hundred Mbps, the office has an ordinary internet connection, traffic must be encrypted, and the company wants a 99.99% availability SLA for the connection. Which option should it choose?

stem: A retailer's users are all in one country near its Google Cloud region. stem: Three engineers run terraform apply for the same Google Cloud environment from their own laptops. Each laptop keeps its own terraform.tfstate, and runs keep trying to recreate resources that a colleague already created. What should the team change?

Delete the resources and let Terraform recreate them after the data is copied elsewhere
Write matching resource blocks and import each existing resource into the Terraform state, for example with `terraform import`
Run `terraform apply` with matching resource blocks, which takes over resources of the same name

stem: A small platform team wants to deploy Terraform configurations that live in a Git repository, keep a history of deployments and revisions, and preview what a change would do, all through a Google-managed service. They do not want to run Terraform on engineers' laptops or operate their own build servers. Which service fits?

choices.text: Config Connector, which applies Terraform files from Git to a Cloud Storage bucket through a Kubernetes controller
Cloud Run functions, which run Terraform inside an HTTP function triggered by commits to the repository
Cloud Deployment Manager, which deploys YAML templates and is supported for new deployments
Infrastructure Manager, which runs Terraform configurations as managed deployments with revisions and previews

stem: Users report that VM `app-1` in subnet `web` cannot connect to TCP port 5432 on VM `db-1` in subnet `data` of the same VPC network. The engineer wants to find out which firewall rule or route blocks the traffic, without logging in to either VM or generating real traffic first. Which tool fits best?

choices.text: Connectivity Tests, with `app-1` as source, `db-1` as destination, TCP and port 5432
Cloud Asset Inventory, which lists the firewall rules and shows which of them is applied last
Cloud Profiler, which samples the CPU usage of the database process to show why connections fail and where
Cloud Trace, which follows the request from `app-1` to `db-1` and marks the slowest network hop

stem: VMs in the VPC network `prod-vpc` must resolve names under `corp.example.com.` using the company's on-premises DNS server at 10.200.0.53. The data center is connected to the VPC network with HA VPN. Names in other domains should still be resolved by Google Cloud as before. What should be configured?

choices.text: An inbound server policy on `prod-vpc`, so that the on-premises server is queried first for every name in the VPC network
A public Cloud DNS managed zone for `corp.example.com.` with an NS record that points to 10.200.0.53
A Cloud NAT gateway with a rule that translates DNS queries for `corp.example.com.` to 10.200.0.53
A private Cloud DNS forwarding zone for `corp.example.com.` authorized for `prod-vpc`, with 10.200.0.53 as the forwarding target

stem: A cost review suggests that the project `legacy-apps` contains reserved static external IP addresses that are not attached to anything. An engineer wants to list them and release those no longer needed. Which approach is correct?

choices.text: Reserved addresses expire automatically after 30 days without use, so the engineer only needs to wait
Ephemeral addresses are released only when the project is deleted, so the engineer should delete the entire project
Run `gcloud compute addresses list`, keep status RESERVED, and release the unneeded ones with `delete`
Run `gcloud compute instances list` and delete every VM that has no external IP address attached to it

stem: The VPC network `hub-vpc` has a custom static route to the on-premises range 192.168.0.0/16 through a VPN tunnel. `spoke-vpc` is peered with `hub-vpc` and cannot reach 192.168.0.0/16, although VMs in the two networks reach each other. The engineer wants spoke VMs to use that route. What is needed?

choices.text: Create a second peering from `spoke-vpc` to the on-premises network, because routes are shared through peering of data centers
Enable export of custom routes on the hub side and import of custom routes on the spoke side of the peering
Recreate the peering as a Shared VPC attachment, because peered networks never exchange any routes
Add a firewall rule in `spoke-vpc` that allows egress to 192.168.0.0/16, which makes the route appear in its route table

stem: A regulator requires that audit exports in `gs://acme-audit` cannot be deleted or overwritten for seven years, and that even project owners cannot shorten or remove this rule once it is in place. Which TWO actions meet the requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Lock the retention policy, which permanently prevents reducing or removing it
Set a lifecycle rule that moves objects to Archive after seven years
Enable Object Versioning with a lifecycle rule that deletes noncurrent versions after seven years
Give only the audit team the Storage Object Admin role on the bucket
Set a bucket retention policy with a retention period of seven years

stem: A data team sets a default table expiration of 7 days on the existing BigQuery dataset `staging`, which already contains 20 tables with no expiration. Which TWO statements about this setting are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Expired tables can only be recovered by restoring the whole dataset from a backup, never individually
New tables created in the dataset after the change get a 7-day expiration unless the table is created with its own expiration
A table created with its own expiration still expires after 7 days, because the dataset default always wins
All 20 existing tables are scheduled to be deleted exactly seven days after the setting is saved
Tables already in the dataset keep their current expiration settings and do not expire because of the new default

stem: The Cloud SQL for MySQL instance `orders-db` has automatic storage increases turned off, and writes now fail because the disk is full. The team wants the writes to work again, and wants the instance to avoid this problem in the future without regular manual resizing. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Turn on point-in-time recovery so that old transaction logs are removed and the data files shrink
Recreate the instance with a smaller disk after exporting the data, which frees up space
Enlarge the disk and run `gcloud sql instances patch orders-db --storage-auto-increase`
Enable high availability, because the standby instance adds extra storage capacity to the primary

stem: All employees of the company use Cloud Identity accounts in the domain `example.com`. The company wants every employee to be able to view the contents of one Cloud Storage bucket `gs://acme-handbook`, and nobody outside the company. Which principal should receive the Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket?

choices.text: `allUsers`, which is restricted to members of the organization when public access prevention is off
The project's `default` service account, which employees can use to open the bucket
`allAuthenticatedUsers`, which means all signed-in accounts of the company
`domain:example.com`, which represents all users in that Cloud Identity or Workspace domain

stem: A reporting group needs to read objects from exactly one bucket, `gs://acme-exports`, in project `data-prod`, which holds 30 other buckets with sensitive data. The security team wants the narrowest practical grant. Which command is best?

choices.text: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding data-prod --member="group:reporting@example.com" --role="roles/viewer"`
`gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding data-prod --member="group:reporting@example.com" --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"`
`gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://acme-exports --member="group:reporting@example.com" --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"`
`gcloud organizations add-iam-policy-binding 1234 --member="group:reporting@example.com" --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"`

stem: A trainer wants an intern to see which VM instances, disks and networks exist in project `training-lab`, but the intern must not be able to create, change or delete anything, and need not see data inside Cloud Storage or BigQuery. Which role is most appropriate on the project?

choices.text: Compute Viewer (`roles/compute.viewer`), which gives read-only access to Compute Engine resources
Compute Admin (`roles/compute.admin`), which gives full control of Compute Engine resources
Storage Admin (`roles/storage.admin`), which lets the intern view every bucket and object in the project
Service Account User (`roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`), which lets the intern view the resources that service accounts can run

stem: A company is defining IAM practices for a growing engineering team. Which TWO practices follow Google Cloud's IAM recommendations? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Give service accounts the Owner role on the project so that deployment automation never fails because of permissions
Grant roles to Google groups that match job functions, so access changes when people join or leave
Grant each required role to individual users on every project, because group membership can lag behind
Grant the Editor role at the organization level to all engineers so that new projects need no IAM work
Apply least privilege by granting predefined roles with only the permissions needed, at the lowest practical level

stem: Before an audit, the security lead wants a short list of all principals that hold the Owner role on project `shop-prod`. The project's allow policy is a long document with many roles and members. Which command prints one line per member for just that role?

choices.text: `gcloud iam roles describe roles/owner --flatten="includedPermissions" --format="value(includedPermissions)" --quiet`
`gcloud projects describe shop-prod --format="table(bindings.members)"`
`gcloud iam service-accounts list --project=shop-prod --filter="role:roles/owner" --format="value(email)"`
`gcloud projects get-iam-policy shop-prod --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.role:roles/owner" --format="value(bindings.members)"`

stem: Analysts run ad-hoc queries on the BigQuery dataset `clickstream` under on-demand pricing. Last month one careless query scanned several terabytes. The data lead wants a safeguard so that a single query fails before running when it would read more than 500 GB, without incurring a charge for it. What should the analysts use?

choices.text: A default table expiration of one day on the dataset, which deletes tables that are scanned too often
Table preview, which reads rows at no charge and stops any query that is larger than the preview
The maximum bytes billed setting on the query, for example `bq query --maximum_bytes_billed=500000000000`
A dry run of every query, which blocks any query that would read more than the allowed amount

stem: Monitoring shows that a service account key of `deploy-sa` was accidentally committed to a public Git repository an hour ago. The key is used by a CI job that the team wants to keep working through a quick fix. What should the engineer do first?

choices.text: Delete the project that contains `deploy-sa`, since only that step invalidates every key of the account
Rename `deploy-sa` so that the key file no longer matches the name of the account it was issued for
Delete the Git repository so nobody can copy the key any more, and keep using the same key in the CI job afterwards
Disable the exposed key with `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable`, give the CI job a new credential, then delete the key

stem: The service account `sync-sa@proj-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com` runs a job in project `proj-a`. The job must read the value of one Secret Manager secret, `partner-api-key`, which lives in project `proj-b`, and must not reach anything else in `proj-b`. What is the least-privilege way to give it access?

choices.text: Create a new service account in `proj-b`, download its key, and give the key file to the job in `proj-a`
Grant `sync-sa@proj-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role on the secret `partner-api-key` in `proj-b`
Move the job's VM to `proj-b`, because service accounts can only be used by principals in their own project
Grant `sync-sa@proj-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the Owner role on `proj-b`, because service accounts of other projects cannot be given narrower roles

stem: An organization enforces the boolean constraint `compute.requireOsLogin` in a policy at the organization node. Lab projects are spread over many folders and must stay where they are, and each lab project has the tag `env=lab` bound at project level. The security team wants OS Login enforcement turned off for lab projects only, including lab projects created next month, without maintaining a policy on each project. What is the approach with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Add the lab teams to an IAM deny policy exception for the constraint, so that OS Login is not required when they work in lab projects
Set a project-level policy with enforcement off on each existing lab project, and add the same step to the runbook for new lab projects
Move every lab project into a new Lab folder and set a folder-level policy there that turns enforcement of the constraint off for that folder
Add a tag condition to the organization-level policy that turns enforcement off for resources tagged env=lab and keeps it on for everything else

stem: The platform team must stop anyone in the organization from creating GKE node pools that have node auto-upgrade turned off. No predefined constraint covers this field, the request must be refused before the node pool exists, and the rule must cover every current and future project. A proposal for a scheduled job that deletes non-compliant node pools after the fact has already been rejected by security. What should the team do?

choices.text: Remove the Kubernetes Engine Admin role from all developers, and let only the platform team create node pools after reviewing each request by hand
Attach an IAM deny policy at the organization that denies the node pool create permission to every principal except the members of the platform group
Define a custom organization policy constraint with a CEL condition on the node pool's auto-upgrade field, and enforce it in a policy at the organization
Create a Cloud Asset Inventory real-time feed for node pool changes and notify the security team through Pub/Sub whenever auto-upgrade is turned off

stem: A data team of 25 analysts queries BigQuery in project `ana-prod` with on-demand pricing. Finance wants each analyst limited to 2 TiB of data processed per day and the whole project to 30 TiB per day, with queries over a limit failing instead of only sending a notification. Analysts run many small queries, so a cap on each single query is not enough. Which TWO settings should the engineer configure? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A BigQuery reservation with a fixed number of slots assigned to ana-prod, so that the project can never process more than 30 TiB a day
A Cloud Billing budget scoped to the BigQuery service with thresholds at 50% and 90%, sending alerts to the data lead and the analysts
A maximum bytes billed of 2 TiB in each analyst's query settings, so that any analyst who processes more than that in a day is refused
A custom quota override on ana-prod for Query usage per day per user, set to 2 TiB, so each analyst and service account is limited separately
A custom quota override on ana-prod for Query usage per day, set to 30 TiB, so the project as a whole stops processing above that amount

stem: On Monday an engineer ran `gcloud projects delete web-stage` by mistake; today is Thursday. The project held VMs, a Cloud SQL instance and some Cloud Storage buckets, and it was linked to the company's billing account. The team wants the project back under the same project ID as quickly as possible and wants to know what to expect afterwards. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The project ID is released at shutdown, so the team must create a new project named web-stage and rebuild its resources from backups
After the restore, the project must be linked to the billing account again, because shutdown disconnects billing and restore does not reinstate it
Restoring brings back every Cloud Storage object and Pub/Sub resource exactly as it was, because all services keep data for 30 days
Only Cloud Customer Care can restore a deleted project, so the team must open a support case and wait for Google to restore it
Within the 30-day recovery period, a principal with the project undelete permission can run `gcloud projects undelete web-stage` to restore it

stem: A company wants every project under the Prod folder, including projects created later, to be marked as production so that an IAM allow policy condition can grant the on-call group extra roles only on production resources. The marker must be set once on the folder and flow down automatically, and changing it must require a dedicated IAM role rather than ordinary edit rights on the project. What should the engineer use?

choices.text: A tag key env with the value prod bound to the Prod folder, referenced with resource.matchTag in the conditional role binding
A label env=prod set on the Prod folder, referenced in the binding's condition through resource.labels so that new projects inherit it
A label env=prod added to each project by the project creation script, referenced by a condition that reads the project's labels
A network tag prod added to all VMs through their instance templates, referenced by the IAM condition through each VM's resource name

stem: A startup runs a public demo on Cloud Run in project `demo-web`, which also hosts a VM and a Cloud SQL instance used by other teams. If the month's Cloud Run spend in the project goes past an agreed amount, new Cloud Run usage must stop automatically until someone reviews it, while the VM and the database keep running. Nobody on the team wants to write or maintain automation code. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: An alerts-only budget on demo-web with a Pub/Sub topic and a Cloud Run function that disables billing on the project above the amount
A lower Cloud Run request quota in demo-web, sized from the monthly amount so that the service can never cost more than the limit
An alerts-only budget scoped to the Cloud Run service with thresholds at 90% and 100% of actual spend, emailing the project owners
A spend cap budget scoped to the demo-web project and the Cloud Run service, with the monthly amount set to the agreed limit

stem: Several teams share one GKE Standard cluster, each team in its own Kubernetes namespace. Finance wants a monthly SQL report in BigQuery that splits the cluster's cost by namespace, based on the CPU and memory each team's Pods request. The billing account already exports standard usage cost data to BigQuery, and finance does not want to maintain any agents or scripts on the cluster. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Install the Ops Agent on every node, so that it reports each Pod's measured CPU and memory usage to Cloud Billing for the split
Enable the detailed usage cost export for the billing account, because GKE cost allocation data is not part of the standard export
Enable the pricing export for the billing account, because namespace costs are calculated from the list price of the SKUs Pods use
Add a team label to every node pool, because Cloud Billing splits node costs only by the labels set on the node pools of the cluster
Enable GKE cost allocation on the cluster, so the cluster name and each namespace appear as labels on the cost rows in the billing export

stem: All research projects sit in the Research folder and are paid by billing account `RES-01`, except one grant-funded project in the same folder that is paid by a different billing account. New research projects are created almost every week. The finance lead creates one budget on `RES-01`, scoped to the Research folder, with an alert at 80% of a monthly amount. Which statement describes what this budget tracks?

choices.text: Nothing yet, because a folder-scoped budget only starts tracking once every project in the folder uses the same billing account
Only the projects that were in the folder when the budget was created, so each new project has to be added to its scope by hand
Every current and future project in the folder that is paid by RES-01, while the grant-funded project's costs are not counted
Every project in the folder including the grant-funded one, because a folder scope ignores which billing account pays each project

stem: A legacy order-processing application runs on one Compute Engine VM and keeps its queue files on an attached data disk. The application cannot scale out to more VMs. The team wants the VM recreated automatically whenever an application health check fails, and the data disk, its contents and the VM's name must survive every recreation and every later template update. What should the engineer set up?

choices.text: A managed instance group of size one with autohealing and a stateful policy that preserves the data disk, so recreated VMs keep the disk and name
A managed instance group of size one with autohealing, and the queue files moved onto the boot disk that the instance template creates
A standalone VM with automatic restart in its availability policy, plus a daily snapshot schedule attached to the data disk
An unmanaged instance group behind an internal load balancer whose health check restarts the VM whenever the application stops answering

stem: A zonal managed instance group runs 8 web VMs in `us-east1-b`. The project's CPU quota in us-east1 has no room for even one more VM of this type, and a quota increase will take weeks. The team must roll out a new instance template today while at least 7 VMs keep serving at every moment of the update. Which TWO update settings should the engineer use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Set maxSurge to 0, so the group never tries to create an extra VM above the target size while it replaces VMs during the update
Keep the default maxSurge for a zonal group, which creates one new VM before an old one is removed and needs no extra quota
Set the minimal action to RESTART, so the VMs pick up the new template by rebooting in place without being replaced at all
Set maxUnavailable to 0, so no VM ever stops serving and the update replaces each VM only after its replacement is running
Set maxUnavailable to 1, so the group takes only one VM out of service at a time and at least 7 of the 8 keep serving

stem: An engineer creates an instance schedule in `europe-west1` that stops dev VMs at 19:00 and starts them at 07:00 in the team's time zone, and attaches it to five VMs in that region that use only standard persistent disks. The next morning all five VMs are still running from the day before, and nobody started them by hand. The engineer holds Compute Instance Admin (v1) on the project. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Instance schedules act only on VMs created after the schedule exists, so the five existing VMs must be recreated from their template
Instance schedules always run in UTC and ignore the selected time zone, so the stop operation will simply happen hours later than planned
The project's Compute Engine Service Agent lacks a role with the start and stop permissions, which the schedule needs to act on the VMs
The engineer needs Compute Instance Admin (v1) at the organization level, because schedules are checked against organization policies

stem: A Cloud Run service receives webhooks, returns HTTP 202 immediately, and then keeps processing the payload in a background goroutine for about 20 seconds. In production much of that background work stalls or never finishes, although it completes on a developer's laptop. The service still uses default settings, and its traffic is steady throughout the day. What should the engineer change to make the background work reliable?

choices.text: Raise the maximum concurrency per instance to 1,000, so each instance accepts more webhooks while earlier work finishes in the background
Switch the service to instance-based billing, so CPU stays allocated to each instance outside of request processing as well
Raise the service's request timeout to 60 minutes, so that background goroutines can keep running after the response is sent
Set a minimum number of instances, so that idle instances stay warm and are not shut down while background work is still running

stem: An engineer runs `gcloud container clusters create shop --region=us-central1 --num-nodes=3`, expecting three nodes for a small app. Creation fails with an error that the regional in-use IP address quota is exceeded. Nodes get external IP addresses, the cluster uses three zones of the region, and the project's in-use IP address quota in us-central1 is 8. The team wants to keep a regional control plane. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Use --zone instead of --region, because --num-nodes is per region and the control plane replicas also use external IPs
Use --num-nodes=2, because a regional cluster adds one spare node per zone for upgrades on top of the requested count
Request a regional in-use IP quota increase first, because regional clusters always need at least nine nodes to be created
Use --num-nodes=1, because in a regional cluster the value is per zone, so three zones give three nodes in total

stem: A research institute must move 600 TB of archived imaging data from its data center to Cloud Storage within 6 weeks. Its only internet link is 1 Gbps, and about half of it is used by daily work that must not be disrupted. Assume 1 Gbps moves about 10 TB per day at full speed. The data will not change during the move. Which approach is the MOST practical?

choices.text: Set up Cloud VPN to the VPC network and copy the data through the tunnel, since VPN traffic does not count against the internet link
Run `gcloud storage cp -r` from several servers at once over the existing link, with most of the copying scheduled for nights and weekends
Order a Transfer Appliance, copy the data onto it in the data center, and ship it back so that Google uploads the data to the bucket
Use Storage Transfer Service with on-premises agents limited to the free half of the link, copying the data in parallel streams

stem: Point-of-sale devices publish JSON sales events to a Pub/Sub topic whose schema matches the columns of the BigQuery table `sales.events`. The data team wants each event in that table within seconds, with no transformation or aggregation, at-least-once delivery is acceptable, and messages that cannot be written must be kept for review. The team wants the LEAST operational overhead. What should the engineer set up?

choices.text: A BigQuery subscription on the topic that writes into sales.events using the table schema, with a dead-letter topic attached to it
A push subscription to a Cloud Run service that streams each event into sales.events and logs failed rows to Cloud Logging
A Cloud Storage subscription that writes files every minute, followed by a scheduled BigQuery load job from the bucket into the table
A Dataflow streaming job built from the Pub/Sub to BigQuery template, with a dead-letter table for the rows that fail to insert

stem: A 4 TB order database runs on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in us-east1 with high availability enabled. A new policy requires that, if the whole region becomes unavailable, the team can bring up a writable copy in us-west1 within one hour and lose at most a few minutes of data. Restoring the nightly backups takes several hours. What should the engineer add to the setup?

choices.text: Point-in-time recovery with seven days of logs, so that a new instance can be restored in us-west1 at the moment of the outage
An hourly export of the database to a dual-region Cloud Storage bucket, imported into a new instance in us-west1 after a failure
A standby in us-west1 for the high-availability configuration, so that the automatic failover moves the primary to the other region
A cross-region read replica in us-west1, which the team promotes to a standalone primary instance if us-east1 becomes unavailable

stem: Internal clients in `us-central1` must reach two backend groups through one private IP address: requests to `/api/*` go to one managed instance group and requests to `/static/*` to another. Clients and backends are in the same region of a custom mode VPC network, nothing may be exposed to the internet, and routing must be based on the URL path. Which TWO steps are part of the solution? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud Armor rules that allow only the internal client ranges to reach it
Create a regional internal Application Load Balancer whose URL map sends each path prefix to its own backend service
Create a Cloud NAT gateway in us-central1, so the backends can send responses back to the internal clients through the load balancer
Create an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer with two forwarding rules, one for each path prefix, on the same IP address
Create a proxy-only subnet in us-central1 of the network, which provides the addresses the load balancer's Envoy proxies use

stem: A company connects its data center to a VPC network through one HA VPN gateway with dynamic routing on a Cloud Router. The on-premises VPN device has a single public IP address. Today one tunnel runs from interface 0 of the HA VPN gateway to that address, and the network team learns that the setup does not qualify for the 99.99% availability SLA. What should the team change?

choices.text: Buy a second public IP address for the on-premises device first, because the 99.99% SLA needs two peer addresses on that side
Add a second tunnel from interface 1 of the HA VPN gateway to the same peer address, with its own BGP session on the Cloud Router
Add a second Cloud Router in the region and attach it to the existing tunnel, so that two routers protect the single BGP session
Replace the HA VPN gateway with a Classic VPN gateway using static routes, since Classic VPN gives the higher SLA with one peer address

stem: A Cloud Run service in `europe-west1` must connect to a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance that has only a private IP address in the VPC network `core`, reached through private services access. Security forbids a public IP on the instance, the service and the instance are in the same project, and the team does not want any connector instances or other VMs to manage. What should the engineer configure for the Cloud Run service?

choices.text: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy built into Cloud Run, connecting through the instance's public IP address with IAM database authentication
A Cloud NAT gateway on the core network with a static IP, and that address added to the authorized networks of the instance
A Serverless VPC Access connector in the core network, sized with two connector instances, and the instance's private IP as the target
Direct VPC egress to a subnet of the core network, and connect from the code to the instance's private IP address on port 3306

stem: An engineer supports two clients, each with its own Google account, organization, default project and default region. Several times a day she switches between them in the same terminal, and twice she has run commands against the wrong client's project. She wants to switch account, project and region together with one command, and occasionally run a single command for the other client without switching. What should she use?

choices.text: Two separate Cloud Shell tabs, one for each client, because every Cloud Shell tab keeps its own signed-in account and gcloud settings
One configuration, with `gcloud auth login` and `gcloud config set project` run before each switch and wrapped in a shell alias
Two named gcloud configurations, switched with `gcloud config configurations activate`, and the `--configuration` flag for one-off commands
Two service account keys, one per client, activated with `gcloud auth activate-service-account` whenever she moves between clients

stem: A retailer runs a GKE Standard cluster on the Regular release channel. For a 10-week holiday period, workloads must not be evicted by automatic node upgrades and the cluster's Kubernetes minor version must not change, but the security team still wants control plane patch upgrades to be applied automatically during that time. What should the engineer configure for the holiday period?

choices.text: A maintenance exclusion with the "No minor or node upgrades" scope that covers the whole 10-week period, set on the cluster
A maintenance exclusion with the "No minor upgrades" scope that covers the whole 10-week period, set on the cluster
A maintenance exclusion with the default "No upgrades" scope that covers the whole 10-week period, set on the cluster
A maintenance window limited to Sunday nights from 01:00 to 05:00, with node auto-upgrade left on for every node pool

stem: An engineer grows `data-1`, a 500 GB balanced Persistent Disk attached as a secondary disk with an ext4 file system and no partition table, to 1 TB with `gcloud compute disks resize`. The command succeeds and `lsblk` on the Linux VM shows the device as 1 TB, but `df -h` still shows about 500 GB for its mount point. The application must not be stopped. What should the engineer do next?

choices.text: Detach the disk and attach it again with the gcloud detach-disk and attach-disk commands, so that the guest reports the new size
Run `gcloud compute disks resize` once more with the same size, because the first call only updated the disk's metadata record
Restart the VM, because Compute Engine extends the file systems of secondary disks automatically while the guest operating system boots
Run `sudo resize2fs` on the device while it stays mounted, because the file system on a non-boot disk must be extended manually

stem: A VM running `n2-standard-8` must move to `c3-standard-8` for better performance. The engineer stops the VM and runs `gcloud compute instances set-machine-type`, but the change is not allowed. The VM is not part of a managed instance group and has no Local SSD, and the engineer holds Compute Instance Admin (v1) on the project. The team wants to keep the data on the VM's disks. What explains the failure, and what should the engineer do?

choices.text: Moving from a second generation series such as N2 to a third generation series such as C3 needs a new VM, built by following the move-workload procedure
The machine type can only be changed while the VM is running, so the engineer should start the VM and repeat the same set-machine-type command
Changing the machine type needs Compute Admin at the organization level, so the engineer should request that role before trying again
C3 machine types need a larger boot disk than N2, so the engineer should resize the boot disk first and then repeat the set-machine-type command

stem: A company runs Cloud SQL for MySQL instances for staging and production.
