Since then the export fails with HTTP 403 and the message `The service account does not have the required permissions for the bucket.` Running `gcloud sql instances describe orders-db --format="value(serviceAccountEmailAddress)"` returns `p123456789-abc123@gcp-sa-cloud-sql.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Security wants the narrowest change. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Grant Storage Object Admin on the acme-db-exports bucket to the instance's service account shown in serviceAccountEmailAddress
Grant Storage Object Admin on the project that hosts orders-db to the instance's service account shown in serviceAccountEmailAddress
Grant Storage Object Admin on the whole backup-prod project to backup-runner, because bucket-level grants do not cover exports
Grant backup-runner Service Account Token Creator on the instance's service account, so the export writes with backup-runner's identity

stem: The managed instance group `crawler` in us-central1 runs VMs without external IPs. Its Public NAT gateway uses manual NAT IP assignment with 2 static addresses and static port allocation with a minimum of 2,048 ports per VM, set months ago because busy VMs need that many. Each NAT IP provides 64,512 source ports. This week the autoscaler grew the group from 50 to 70 VMs; 8 of the new VMs cannot reach the internet, and NAT error logs show `allocation_status: DROPPED` for packets from them, while all other VMs work. Busy VMs must not start dropping connections. Which TWO changes would each, on its own, fix the problem? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Lower the minimum ports per VM from 2,048 to 64, so that the two existing NAT addresses can serve up to 1,008 VMs each
Reserve two more static addresses and add them to the gateway's manual NAT IP list, keeping the minimum of 2,048 ports per VM
Raise the maximum size of the crawler group's autoscaler, so that the autoscaler can add VMs that have their own external IPs
Turn on endpoint-independent mapping on the gateway, so that each VM reuses the same NAT port for different destinations
Switch the gateway to automatic NAT IP allocation, so that Google Cloud adds NAT addresses as more VMs need ports, keeping 2,048 ports per VM

stem: The Ops Agent was installed by an agent policy on 20 Linux VMs. Syslog entries from all of them appear in Logs Explorer, but agent metrics such as `agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used` are missing for 6 VMs created last week from a new template that uses the service account `batch-sa`. On those VMs every Ops Agent service is active, the access scope is `cloud-platform`, and the agent's own logs repeat permission-denied errors for `monitoring.timeSeries.create`. `batch-sa` holds Logs Writer on the project. The other 14 VMs use `app-sa`, which holds Logs Writer and Monitoring Metric Writer. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Reinstall the Ops Agent on the six VMs with the agent policy, so that its metrics configuration is created again from scratch
Change the access scopes of the six VMs to the monitoring write scope only, so that the agent's requests carry a metrics token
Grant Monitoring Metric Writer to the Compute Engine default service account, which the Ops Agent uses for metrics on every VM
Grant batch-sa the Monitoring Metric Writer role on the project, so that the agent on those six VMs can write its metrics

stem: Alex left the company in March, and his Cloud Identity account `alex@example.com` was deleted. In September he rejoined and an administrator created a new account with the same address. Alex now cannot query tables in project `analytics`, where he used to have access. Running `gcloud projects get-iam-policy analytics --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.members~alex"` shows the member `deleted:user:alex@example.com?uid=123456789012345678901` in a binding for `roles/bigquery.dataViewer`. His manager says the binding will reattach once the directory sync finishes. Alex should get back exactly the access he had, and the audit trail must show who granted it. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Wait for the directory sync to finish, after which IAM maps the deleted entry to the new account because the email address is the same
Restore the old Cloud Identity account so that its unique ID matches the deleted entry again, then delete the new account Alex is using
Add a Data Viewer binding for user:alex@example.com, as the deleted entry is another principal that never applies to the new account
Grant Alex BigQuery Data Viewer on the organization instead, since project bindings that mention deleted users stay locked for a year

stem: The Prod folder has an IAM deny policy with one rule: denied principals `principalSet://goog/public:all`, denied permission `compute.googleapis.com/instances.delete`, exception principal `group:prod-breakglass@example.com`, and the denial condition `resource.matchTag('123456789012/env', 'prod')`. Project `shop-prod` in that folder carries the tag `env=prod`. Sam, an SRE, holds Compute Instance Admin (v1) on `shop-prod` and must delete a stuck VM during tonight's incident. Policy Troubleshooter shows his allow policy grants the permission but the deny policy denies it. Access must last only for the incident, must leave an audit trail, and must not loosen the rule for anyone else. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Remove the env=prod tag from shop-prod during the incident, so that the denial condition is false and Sam's existing role applies again
Add Sam to the prod-breakglass group for the incident, ideally with a membership expiration, since exception principals are exempt from the rule
Add a binding for Sam with a request.time condition ending tonight, because conditional allow bindings are evaluated before deny rules
Grant Sam the Owner role on shop-prod for tonight, because Owner permissions are evaluated before deny policies on the same project

stem: A company keeps every user-managed service account in project `sa-hub`, and workloads run in other projects. An engineer who holds Compute Instance Admin (v1) on project `batch-prod` and Service Account User on `render-sa@sa-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` runs `gcloud compute instances create render-1 --project=batch-prod --zone=us-central1-a --service-account=render-sa@sa-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com --scopes=cloud-platform`. The request fails with an error saying that using service accounts from another project is disabled by the constraint `iam.disableCrossProjectServiceAccountUsage`. Nobody has changed organization policies since the organization was created. Security wants the change limited to the project that owns the accounts and to the one Google service that needs it, without giving the engineer broader rights. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Set a policy on the folder holding sa-hub and batch-prod that stops enforcing iam.disableCrossProjectServiceAccountUsage, covering both projects at once
Grant the engineer Service Account Token Creator on render-sa in place of Service Account User, because attaching across projects needs token creation rights
In sa-hub, set a project-level policy that stops enforcing iam.disableCrossProjectServiceAccountUsage, so its accounts can be attached to resources in other projects
In batch-prod, set a project-level policy that stops enforcing iam.disableCrossProjectServiceAccountUsage, because the constraint is checked where the VM is created
Grant Service Account Token Creator on render-sa to the Compute Engine Service Agent of batch-prod, service-PROJECT_NUMBER@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com

stem: A Cloud Build trigger in project `ci-prod` builds an image and runs `gcloud run deploy orders --image=IMAGE --service-account=orders-run@app-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --region=europe-west1 --project=app-prod`. The trigger runs as the user-specified service account `builder@ci-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, which has Cloud Run Admin on `app-prod`. The step fails with `PERMISSION_DENIED: Permission 'iam.serviceaccounts.actAs' denied on service account orders-run@app-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (or it may not exist)`. The account exists, and an engineer already granted `builder` Service Account User on `builder` itself, which did not help. Security requires that `builder` cannot act as any other service account in `app-prod`. What should the engineer grant?

choices.text: Service Account User to builder on the orders-run service account only, so that builder may attach that one identity to the service
Service Account User to the Cloud Build service agent on orders-run, because the service agent performs the deploy for every trigger
Service Account Token Creator to builder on orders-run, so that builder can create tokens for orders-run during each deployment
Service Account User to builder on the app-prod project, so that builder may attach any service account of the project to the service
